conviction_note: Both measurements are near zero. Q3 should be the first clean quarter after Q2's $2.1M energy-asset loss and expense spike, but the July expense guide makes that mechanical and consensus ($1.05-1.08) already sits on the core run-rate. Deal costs and the 16 Sep Fed hike roughly offset each other. The Century acquisition (25%+ EPS accretion) has been public since 17 Sep and the stock did not react. abs_move is set a little above the 2.4% median because this is the first call since a deal that nearly doubles the balance sheet; p_up is 52.
bar: Q3 2026 diluted EPS consensus of about $1.05-1.08: Earnings Whispers $1.05 and Tickflow $1.08 from 2 analysts (range $1.07-1.08), both read via search snippet https://www.tickflow.io/stock/BSVN/forecast and https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/x/BSVN (the Tickflow page returned HTTP 429 when fetched directly). Revenue is about $25M (Tickflow). The company's own Q3 guide is noninterest expense of $9.5-9.7M and core NIM of 4.45-4.53%, from the Q2 call (https://www.webull.com.au/news-detail/15277049858696192). The two estimate sources roughly agree, so sizes are kept small.
positioning_check: Short interest was 148,008 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, about 1.6% of 9.53M shares outstanding, with 2.56 days to cover (Equibles/FINRA, https://equibles.com/stocks/bsvn/short-interest, read 2026-10-14 by the sweep). Not crowded. There is no options market, so no skew. Spot $55.00 is 4.2% under the 52-week high, run-up is +1.16% over 20 days and -0.24% over 5, and 20-day realised vol is 13.2%: a quiet, low-vol bank stock with no visible positioning.

findings.finding: Q2 2026 diluted EPS of $0.87 (against roughly $1.04 consensus) included a $2.1M pre-tax loss on selling oil and gas properties (10-Q) and noninterest expense of $11.9M (IT remediation plus M&A consulting). Management guided Q3 expense to $9.5-9.7M. With Q2 NII of $21.9M and a normal fee line, Q3 mechanically rebuilds to roughly $1.05-1.13, so the quarter comes in near or slightly above the $1.05-1.08 bar on a core basis.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 EPS miss ($0.87 vs ~$1.04): -2.51%. Q1 2026 net income $12.01M, up 16% y/y: +2.40%. Reactions are small and follow the EPS headline.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the expense guide is public and consensus already sits on the core run-rate. What is left is NIM: June core NIM was 4.51% and Q2 reported NIM 4.81%, and loan-fee income is lumpy and moves EPS by several cents. If the market expected a clear beat, the stock would have run into the print; it is +1.2% over 20 days.
findings.independence: Q2 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001746129/000114036126028609/ef20078094_ex99-1.htm (same company, a different document) and the Q2 call summary https://www.webull.com.au/news-detail/15277049858696192 for the expense guide.

findings.finding: In September the Century transaction grew from a $68M stalking-horse bid for 71% (1 Jul) to a $91M winning auction bid (3 Sep), then to a whole-company merger ($70M cash plus 1,232,657 shares, ~$137.3M, signed 16 Sep) with KBW and Nelson Mullins as advisors. The $9.5-9.7M Q3 expense guide was given on 16 Jul, before the auction and the merger agreement, so Q3 GAAP expense likely runs above it on deal-related legal and advisory costs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 miss came partly on elevated expense (M&A consulting plus IT remediation, $11.9M against $9.7M a year earlier): -2.51%.
findings.why_not_priced: No estimate source shows a Q3 merger-cost line. If two analysts had raised their expense lines after 16 Sep, the consensus would have drifted down from the ~$1.04 Q2 level, and it has not. It is small because bank investors usually adjust deal costs out, and success fees typically land at closing (Nov), not in Q3.
findings.independence: Auction 8-K https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1746129/000114036126036192/ef20081805_8k.htm (price raised to $88.96M net). The deal itself is the same fact family as the deal-approval finding, but the two land on different lines: Q3 cost here, forward guide there.

findings.finding: The Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sep 2026, the first hike since 2023. Bank7's CFO said on the Q2 call that a hike 'we would benefit from... from an asset sensitive perspective' (deposit cost 2.28-2.30%, about $220M cash). The Q3 call's Q4 NIM outlook could therefore come above the 4.45-4.53% core range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior: on recent calls management guided NIM down (Q2 NIM 4.81% vs 4.96%) and the Q2 print fell 2.51%. There is no history of a NIM raise to compare against.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the hike was a near coin flip beforehand (~50-57% odds) and is a macro fact every bank holder sees. The company-specific part, the size of a NIM raise at a ~4.5% core-NIM, asset-sensitive bank, is not quantified anywhere public. If it were priced, BSVN would have moved after 16 Sep; the stock sat near the $54.57 10-day average.
findings.independence: This is a macro-to-company proxy: the company described its asset sensitivity in the Q2 call summary https://www.webull.com.au/news-detail/15277049858696192, but has not confirmed a number since the hike. The hike itself is single-sourced through secondary outlets (see the search results).

findings.finding: On 9 Oct Bank7 filed an 8-K: Century shareholders approved the merger, the Federal Reserve and the New Mexico FID gave approval or non-objection, and closing is expected 'on or about November 1, 2026'. The Q3 call is therefore the first chance for management to firm pro-forma 2027 numbers. The deal deck already showed 25%+ EPS accretion, ~11% TBV dilution, a 1.7-year earnback and 6.3x P/E with synergies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior deal of this scale (it nearly doubles assets to ~$3.3B). The stock barely moved on the 17 Sep merger announcement (10-day average $54.57 before it, $55.00 now).
findings.why_not_priced: The accretion numbers are public, and the stock's lack of reaction says the market is either sceptical or has not done the work. Faster-than-expected approvals (closing about 6 weeks after signing) remove timing risk. Detail on purchase-accounting marks against Century's ~3.75% cost of funds could swing the reception either way.
findings.independence: Merger deck https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1746129/000114036126036855/ef20081983_ex99-2.htm. It is the same transaction as the merger-cost finding, which is sized on the Q3 cost line, not the forward guide.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call management flagged 'significant loan pay downs' to overcome in H2, with Q3 fundings expected at about double Q2 and mid-single-digit full-year loan growth. Gross loans fell $9.2M in H1 (to $1,600.1M) and WTI traded around $100 in mid-September, so cash-rich energy and commercial borrowers could keep paying down. That risks a flat or lower loan balance, partly offset by prepayment-fee income.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026, with loans down slightly on the half year: -2.51%. That move came mainly on the EPS miss.
findings.why_not_priced: It is inside what management warned of, so mostly priced. The open question is whether fundings matched the 'double' claim, which nothing public measures.
findings.independence: The oil level is a proxy: https://www.psuconnect.in/market/crude-oil-price-today-14-september-2026-wti-trades-near-102-58-amid-supply-jitters (WTI near $102.58 on 14 Sep 2026). The loan balance comes from the 10-Q, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001746129/000114036126032024/bsvn-20260630.htm.

findings.finding: Insiders sold in small size after the Q2 print: CEO Travis 6,500 shares (22 Jul) and Jason Estes about 7,500 shares over 21 Jul-4 Aug. Annual awards were granted on 29 Jul. There have been no insider purchases since and no Form 4s since 4 Aug.
findings.why_not_priced: Public and small, under 0.2% of shares. It is filed for the panel's completeness and carries no expected effect.
findings.independence: Form 144s are in the EDGAR filing list (21 Jul, 22 Jul, 3 Aug 2026).

outside_window.finding: The Century merger closes on or about 2026-11-01. Purchase-accounting marks, the funding of the $70M cash leg, and the 2027 run-rate show up only at and after closing.

searched_and_found_nothing: EDGAR filings since the Q2 10-Q: only the four Century 8-Ks (3 Sep, 10 Sep, 17 Sep, 9 Oct); no capital raise, no sub-debt prospectus, no credit-event 8-K
News search for Bank7 in October 2026: only the call-timing PR (6 Oct) and the earlier dividend raise to $0.30
No analyst note after the deal: only the 17 Jul targets were found (Piper $61, KBW $56); KBW is the deal advisor
Peer read-through: no Oklahoma/Texas community bank print after 16 Jul found that bears on Bank7
Credit: the 10-Q gives no nonaccrual or classified data in the readable excerpt; zero provision and $60K net recoveries in Q2

rejected_candidates.candidate: Quarterly dividend raised 11.11% to $0.30 (record 18 Sep, paid 8 Oct)
rejected_candidates.detail: Announced and paid before the print, so already seen by the market and nothing resolves in the window; the panel may file it as capital_return at 0.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Q2 energy item described as a '$3.7M one-time gain' (call summary and investing.com) against a '$2.1M pre-tax loss on sale' (10-Q)
rejected_candidates.detail: The 10-Q states a $2.1M pre-tax loss on the 10 Apr 2026 sale of oil and gas properties; the 'gain' version from secondary sources was not used for sizing.

baseline_tension: There are no skew and no crowded short to cut against. The findings net slightly positive on a quiet stock 4% under its high, which agrees with the flat run-up: nothing here says the market is wrong.
lessons_applied: Rule 6, inside the guide: the clean-quarter finding lands inside the company's own expense guide, so it moved from +0.2 to +0.1.
Rule 2, one-off below core: deal costs are usually adjusted out by bank investors, so the merger-cost finding moved from -0.3 to -0.2.
Rule 5, macro proxy: the Fed hike is not confirmed by the company since the hike, so it moved from +0.4 to +0.3.
Rule 1, priced fact: the deal accretion is public and the stock did not react on announcement, so the deal-approval finding moved from +0.3 to +0.2.
Rule 5, no information value: the small, old insider sales moved from -0.1 to 0.0.
abs_move_pct and p_up were left unchanged.
